clue.text: King Edward prepared? Too apt!

parts.note: surface reading: a monarch got ready, and the remark is called too fitting
setter's reading: these six letters, crushed and rearranged, spell the vegetable a King Edward is

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a King Edward being made ready is almost too fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: A King Edward is a British variety of potato, not a monarch. The exclamation hints at a reverse anagram: TOO APT, mashed, gives POTATO, so the whole answer describes its own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A King Edward is a common British potato variety, and one that has been boiled and crushed with butter is a classic side dish.

clue.text: Vehicle idled

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low-powered motorbike with pedals
second meaning: the past tense of a verb for drifting about aimlessly and gloomily

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it describes an engine ticking over, but the two words are unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a small motorised bicycle; the verb means sulked or wandered listlessly, the way a bored teenager passes time.

clue.text: I investigate the underworld or Hell — shocks me appallingly

indicators.note: appallingly means dreadfully, so the letters end up in a dreadful jumble

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A first-person speaker probing the criminal world finds it, or something hellish, horribly shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is spoken by the detective, and the underworld is the criminal one, not Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's consulting detective spends his career probing London's criminal classes, its so-called underworld.

clue.text: Study old-time retired leader

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so the parts are read backwards

parts.note: a study or den is a private retreat, a lair
O is a standard abbreviation for old
tide is an old word for time, as in Yuletide

explanation.surface: Someone researches a former head who has stepped down long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old-time' looks like one adjective but splits into two pieces. In British newspapers a leader is the editor's opinion column.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article giving the paper's own opinion is called a leader in Britain, the same thing as this piece.

clue.text: Python lacking a python's core support

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the named letter is dropped from the comedian's name

parts.note: Michael Palin was a member of the Monty Python comedy team
the letter that is removed

indicators.note: a core is the very centre of something, so only the middle letters are taken

parts.note: the two central letters of the word python

explanation.surface: A snake missing part of its middle is described as a prop.
explanation.walkthrough: The first Python is a Monty Python member, the second the snake. PALIN without A is PLIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the base block or pedestal on which a statue or column rests, so it is a physical support.

clue.text: Sport broadcast just after poet

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so the words are judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: a racket game, said quickly
soon means shortly after, said in a clipped way

explanation.surface: A sports programme goes out on air straight after a poetry slot.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, 'tennis soon' runs together into the poet's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Queen Victoria's Poet Laureate, author of The Charge of the Light Brigade.

clue.text: Letter written long ago with quill?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an Old English runic letter for the th sound
second meaning: a sharp spine, as a quill on a porcupine is

explanation.surface: An ancient letter was penned with a feather pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes quill a pen, but it is a spike; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The rune þ was used in Old English writing, and a prickle or spine on a plant is another sense of the same word.

clue.text: Invading yuppies infect compound with rigatoni

definitions.note: a phrase for the process; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: to compound is to mix things together, so the letters are blended into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Young professionals moving in bring their trendy pasta, spreading it through the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the process loosely; yuppies are young upwardly mobile professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: When affluent newcomers move into a poorer district, renovate it and push up prices, the process is given this name.

clue.text: Dodgy leases in empty buildings with no foundations

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the shell of the other word
emptied of its insides, the word keeps only its outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of buildings

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable or crooked, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shady tenancy agreements are found in vacant buildings that lack proper footings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With no foundations' suits the buildings in the surface, but it means unfounded, as an accusation can be.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim without grounds or supporting evidence is unfounded, literally lacking a base to stand on.

clue.text: Prince Oscar is all about getting things just so

indicators.note: all about suggests scattered every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal named Oscar is a perfectionist who needs everything exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is all about' reads as 'is concerned with', but 'all about' is the mixing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Exactness and accuracy, doing a job to the finest detail, is what the noun describes.

clue.text: Sacred word such as amen's first and last

parts.note: om is the sacred syllable chanted in Hindu and Buddhist practice
e.g. is the abbreviation for 'for example'

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that precedes it

parts.note: the opening letter of amen

explanation.surface: A holy word like amen marks both beginning and end of a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and last' look like a pair, but 'first' works on amen and 'last' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The final letter of the Greek alphabet stands for the end of anything, as in 'Alpha and Omega'.

clue.text: Spot lion and unicorn heading inside to make deal

indicators.note: inside puts the lion and the letter within the word for spot

parts.note: a spot is a small round mark, a dot
Leo is the lion of the zodiac

indicators.note: a heading is what sits at the top, so only the opening letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of unicorn

explanation.surface: The heraldic lion and unicorn are spotted together, evoking the royal coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The lion and unicorn suggest the royal arms, but the lion is just a star sign and the unicorn gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal cards or rations is to hand them out in portions, which is exactly what the phrasal verb means.

clue.text: At first you're all nervous, giving the Zulu elder a flower

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.words: you're all nervous, giving the Zulu elder
parts.note: the initial letters of these seven words

explanation.surface: Someone nervously presents a flower to a tribal elder.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a flower is often something that flows, a river; this is China's longest.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword convention reads flower as 'flow-er', a thing that flows, so a river; this one crosses China to Shanghai.

clue.text: Feverish convulsion stopped by shock treatment

indicators.note: something stopped has a plug in it, so one word is filled with the other

parts.note: hic is a hiccup, an involuntary spasm
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A patient's fit is brought under control by electric shock therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: The convulsion here is a hiccup, not a seizure, though the surface pairs it neatly with electroconvulsive therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides frantic, the word originally described the flushed, fevered state of consumptive illness.

clue.text: Principal effects of nightcap?

parts.note: a school's principal is its head
personal effects are belongings, one's gear

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what a late-night drink does to them, the head principally.
explanation.walkthrough: A nightcap is first a bedtime drink; the question mark flags it as an example of the answer, a cap worn in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth cap worn in bed is one example of something worn on the head, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Caught erstwhile setter's fancy

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
erstwhile means formerly, once
the setter has, from the setter's point of view I've

explanation.surface: The setter's former crush has been noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' stands for 'setter has', and the setter speaks as I.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something can mean to imagine or form an idea of it, the same as forming a notion in the mind.

clue.text: Leave to go, having settled up in good humour

parts.note: a congé is formal permission to depart

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned round

parts.note: lain is the past participle of lie, to have come to rest

explanation.surface: Permission to leave is granted once the bill has been paid, in a cheerful mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled up' looks like paying a bill; it is a past participle plus the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant, friendly and agreeable company puts people in a good mood, which the adjective describes.

clue.text: In Romeo's home I start to collect speedwell

indicators.note: in places the first and fourth words inside the word for the hometown

parts.note: Romeo lives in Verona in Shakespeare's play
taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the following word means only its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of collect

explanation.surface: Someone at home in Romeo's city starts gathering a wild flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it goes with the home, but it sends the pronoun and letter inside the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is the common name for plants of the genus whose Latin botanical name is this word.

clue.text: Pains besetting ailing hero at Troy

indicators.note: to beset is to surround on all sides, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: pains are aches
ailing means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A sick Trojan War warrior is plagued by pains.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the hero died from a wound to his heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek champion of the Iliad fought outside Troy and killed Hector there before being shot in the heel.

clue.text: Teddy maybe comes back to life?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwear, of which a one-piece teddy is an example
second meaning: a whimsical verb, the opposite of dies

explanation.surface: A cuddly toy bear seems to come alive.
explanation.walkthrough: A teddy here is a woman's one-piece undergarment, not a bear; the question mark covers the invented verb 'un-dies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes are informally called this, and split as un-dies it jokingly means reverses dying.

clue.text: Danger failing to finish chant

indicators.note: not reaching the end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a mantrap is a hidden snare, a danger to walkers

explanation.surface: A hazard that never quite ends becomes a chant.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTRAP loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase repeated over and over in meditation or prayer is an incantation of this kind.

clue.text: Astronomer terribly ill with old age

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are put into a disordered state

parts.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stargazer is very sick in his later years.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the astronomer went blind in his old age.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist improved the telescope and discovered the four largest moons of Jupiter.

clue.text: Spooner's boy left Spain

parts.note: a lad is a boy
L is the abbreviation for left
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Reverend Spooner's son has gone away from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner's' looks like a Spoonerism signal, but it is 'spooner is': a thing that spoons out soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep long-handled serving utensil scoops soup into bowls, so it is jokingly something that spoons.

clue.text: Leave rag-ends, keeping what's modish?

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the letters lie inside the run of words before

parts.note: letters three to nine of these words

explanation.surface: Fashionable people throw away tatty scraps of cloth but keep what is in style.
explanation.walkthrough: Modish means fashionable, but here it is mode-ish: the mode is a kind of statistical average, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The mode, the most frequent value in data, is one type of mean value in statistics alongside median and mean.

clue.text: I pick winners for Bert's mate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the machine that draws Premium Bond prize numbers
second meaning: the Sesame Street puppet who shares a home with Bert

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of choosing winners on behalf of a friend's pal.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme whose monthly prize numbers are generated by a computer with this acronym name.
explanation.definitionFit: The random-number generator chooses Premium Bond prize-winners, and the Muppet roommate of Bert carries the same name.

clue.text: One leaves injured maiden getting better

definitions.note: a phrase meaning improving; the answer is the base verb

indicators.note: injured means damaged, so the remaining letters are knocked out of order
leaves means departs, so that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hurt young woman leaves, recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIDEN without I leaves MADEN to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransitively the verb can mean improve oneself or recover, the sense of growing healthier or reforming.

clue.text: A way to understand things during class

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the morning'
a class is a session of tuition

explanation.surface: Learning how to understand things happens during lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests school, but the answer is knowing without being taught.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping something instinctively, by gut feeling rather than reasoning, is a means of knowing or comprehending.

clue.text: With hollow smile, take silver spear and apprehend immediately

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its inside, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of smile
to take food or medicine is to eat it
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a lance is a long spear

explanation.surface: Smiling emptily, a warrior grabs a silver spear and arrests someone on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehend' suggests arresting, but here it means grasp mentally.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp or recognise something instantly, with one quick look, is what this phrase means.
